subsystems.name: Host organism (chassis)
subsystems.role: the cell that is rewritten to live on carbon dioxide or to make a fuel molecule.
parts: acetogens that already eat waste gases

subsystems.name: Carbon-fixing pathway
subsystems.role: the enzyme chemistry that pulls CO2 into the cell's metabolism.
parts: synthetic CO2-fixing cycles built from many enzymes
energy and electron supply (ATP, NADPH or hydrogen)

subsystems.name: Genetic toolkit
subsystems.role: the instruments used to design, insert and tune new genes.

subsystems.name: Bioreactor and gas delivery
subsystems.role: feeds CO2 to cells fast enough for them to grow.

subsystems.name: Product recovery
subsystems.role: separates the fuel or chemical from water and cells — often the most energy-hungry step.

subsystems.name: Containment and measurement
subsystems.role: keeps modified organisms out of the environment and proves how much carbon was really captured.

buildSteps.title: Choose the target molecule
buildSteps.detail: Decide whether the goal is a fuel, a chemical feedstock or durable stored carbon, because that sets the whole pathway.

buildSteps.title: Design the metabolic route
buildSteps.detail: Map which enzymes are needed to convert CO2 plus an energy source into the product, and which existing genes to delete.

buildSteps.title: Build the DNA
buildSteps.detail: Genes are synthesised chemically and assembled into constructs, then inserted into the host with CRISPR or similar tools.

buildSteps.title: Screen and evolve
buildSteps.detail: Thousands of strains are grown in small wells; the best are repeatedly selected and mutated to improve growth and yield.

buildSteps.title: Prove it in a bioreactor
buildSteps.detail: The winning strain runs in a litre-scale reactor where gas supply, pH and temperature are controlled.

buildSteps.title: Close the carbon balance
buildSteps.detail: Measure CO2 in, product out and energy used, to check that the process stores more carbon than it emits.

buildSteps.title: Scale up
buildSteps.detail: Move to cubic-metre reactors, where mixing, gas transfer and contamination become the hard problems.

buildSteps.title: Recover and use the product
buildSteps.detail: Separate the fuel or chemical, then burn it, sell it, or store it permanently depending on the goal.

buildSteps.title: Contain and monitor
buildSteps.detail: Deploy biocontainment, waste treatment and environmental monitoring before any outdoor or large-scale use.

prerequisites.tech: Cheap DNA synthesis and genome editing
prerequisites.why: without fast, low-cost gene construction and CRISPR editing, each strain takes years instead of weeks.
RuBisCO, nature's main CO2-fixing enzyme, is slow; synthetic alternatives have been shown only in test tubes.

prerequisites.tech: Organisms that grow on CO2 alone
prerequisites.why: bacteria engineered to use CO2 as their sole carbon source were reported in 2019, but they grow slowly and need extra energy.
capturing CO2 takes energy; if that energy comes from fossil fuels the climate benefit shrinks or disappears.
releasing engineered organisms at industrial scale needs containment rules that do not yet widely exist.
recovering dilute fuel from water can consume more energy than the fuel contains.

pathway.milestone: engineered enzymes and yeasts already make ethanol and other fuels from crops and from steel-mill waste gases
pathway.unlocks: a working industrial base of fermentation, reactors and product recovery to build on.

pathway.milestone: engineered autotrophs producing chemicals and fuels at pilot scale from concentrated CO2 streams
pathway.unlocks: the first realistic pairing of a CO2 source with a living factory.

pathway.milestone: full life-cycle proof that a plant captures more carbon than the process emits
pathway.unlocks: credible carbon accounting, without which the technology cannot claim a climate benefit.

pathway.milestone: products that lock carbon away for decades, or fuels that displace fossil ones, at commercial scale
pathway.unlocks: a supplement to geological CO2 storage and to electrification, mainly where waste gases and cheap low-carbon energy are both available.
